top_choice_rationale: Base editing turns genome modification into a defined, measurable chemical reaction (hydrolytic deamination of one nucleobase in a narrow window, with no double-strand break). The adenine editor needed TadA to be evolved to act on DNA, which is genuine chemical invention, and the outcome has been reproduced independently for a decade and has reached patients. Komor, Liu and Gaudelli are the three people who made the two editor classes, and the citation stays on the chemical conversion, which separates it from the 2020 CRISPR cleavage prize. P004 follows because it keeps Liu and adds the mature, independently confirmed C-N coupling; P001 is my next choice if base editing is judged biotechnology; P002 follows, since its attribution is contestable and it overlaps the 2023 Medicine prize; P003 is sound but thinly supported; P000 is last because several candidates are mature and substantive.
